blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: West Bengal features unique industries, trade sectors, and recognized Geographical Indication (GI) products.
GI tags safeguard the identity, traditional knowledge, and economic value of West Bengal's distinct regional items.
Promoting GI products strengthens local trade and boosts industrial growth across the state.
Match-the-following questions linking specific GI products to their districts or regions in West Bengal.
Key legal and economic aspects of Geographical Indication tags for state trade and industrial growth.
Identification of agricultural, handicraft, and manufactured goods from West Bengal holding GI certification.
Darjeeling Tea — first product in India to get GI tag (2004)
Darjeeling GI — also covers Darjeeling logo and Darjeeling label
Gobindobhog Rice — aromatic rice from Bardhaman; GI tag
Tulaipanji Rice — fragrant rice from North Bengal; GI tag
Fazli Mango — Malda & Murshidabad; GI tag
Baluchari Saree — Bishnupur, Bankura; handwoven silk; GI tag
Nakshi Kantha — embroidered quilt; WB folk art
Bankura Horse — Bankura; terracotta horse; iconic symbol of WB

cells: [EXAM TIP] Darjeeling Tea was the FIRST product in India to receive a GI (Geographical Indication) tag in 2004. This is one of the most frequently asked facts in WB Police exams.
